title: Add Docker Compose dev stack (app + Qdrant) w/ health checks and resource limits
author: Bruno Silva
body: Summary: Adds a runnable Docker Compose stack for local development of the RAG quickstart (API + ingestion worker) backed by a default vector DB (Qdrant). Includes health checks, dependency ordering (service_healthy), and conservative resource limits so people don’t accidentally melt laptops during first run. This is intended to support the <60 min deploy goal and reduce Support tickets around “it works locally but dies under bigger docs”. Motivation / context: We’ve been recommending “run qdrant locally” in READMEs but the setup diverged between templates and was missing health checks + sane defaults. Dogfooding feedback also showed folks running with unlimited containers and then hitting timeouts/429s due to local contention. This PR standardizes the dev stack and documents expected behavior. What’s included: 1) docker compose stack for RAG template: services: rag-api (FastAPI), rag-worker (ingestion), qdrant (vector store), and an optional redis cache (profile: cache). 2) Health checks: qdrant: GET /readyz; rag-api: GET /healthz; worker: simple “heartbeat file” approach (writes /tmp/worker_healthy after boot + periodic tick; compose checks file existence) so we don’t depend on a bespoke endpoint for a background process. 3) Resource limits: adds cpu/memory limits per service using Compose-supported fields (cpus, mem_limit) for local runs; avoids deploy.resources (ignored by non-swarm). Defaults are tuned for typical laptops while still letting ingestion complete. 4) Port + volume conventions: qdrant data persisted in a named volume; logs to stdout; API on 8000. 5) Docs + dev UX: Makefile targets (make compose-up / compose-down / compose-logs / compose-reset) and README updates; adds .env.compose.example with required env vars (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL) + optional knobs (RAG_QDRANT_URL, INGEST_CONCURRENCY). Notes on Apple Silicon and Docker Desktop memory settings. 6) Security: no secrets committed; .env is ignored; compose example uses placeholders; avoids mounting host home dirs; uses read-only mounts where possible for config. Implementation details: - Compose file lives at templates/python/rag/docker/compose.yaml to keep it near the template, and is referenced from the template README. - Depends-on uses condition: service_healthy to avoid the common “API boots before Qdrant is ready” failure mode. - Worker uses a bounded concurrency default (INGEST_CONCURRENCY=2) and a conservative chunk size; actual ingestion tuning remains documented in the template config section. - Adds explicit timeouts to health checks so Docker doesn’t wedge indefinitely on slow machines. Manual test plan: - docker compose -f templates/python/rag/docker/compose.yaml up --build -d - Wait for healthy: docker compose ps (qdrant + rag-api should be healthy within ~30–60s). - Run ingestion: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/ingest (see README) with sample docs; verify worker logs show progress. - Query: curl http://localhost:8000/query; confirm responses include source citations. - Resource limit smoke: with Docker Desktop memory set to 4GB, ingestion of ~50MB text should complete without the host becoming unresponsive. CI: Adds a lightweight compose validation step (docker compose config) and a smoke job that builds the images and starts the stack, then hits /healthz and /readyz. (No full ingestion run in CI yet—kept to <5 min.) Notes / follow-ups: - Future: optionally add an ‘observability’ profile (otel-collector + tempo/jaeger) once ENG-2846 lands; kept out of this PR to reduce moving pieces. - If we see recurrent “worker unhealthy” confusion, we can add a /healthz endpoint to the worker and deprecate the heartbeat file approach. Screenshots/log excerpts: - qdrant health: GET /readyz -> 200 OK - rag-api health: GET /healthz -> {"status":"ok"} (also returns request_id when provided) Release notes: Adds Docker Compose dev stack for Python RAG quickstart (Qdrant backend) with health checks and resource caps; documented in README. Breaking change: false
commits: Add compose.yaml for python/rag template (api, worker, qdrant, optional redis)
Add health checks + depends_on service_healthy ordering
Docs: update RAG README w/ compose quickstart + troubleshooting
CI: compose config validation + minimal health smoke
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please avoid deploy.resources since it won’t be enforced in local compose; can we use mem_limit/cpus and document that Docker Desktop still needs a global memory setting? Also add timeouts to healthchecks to avoid long hangs on slow machines.
Bruno Silva (author): Updated to cpus + mem_limit and added a README note about Docker Desktop memory. Added timeout + retries for qdrant and api health checks.
Marcus Lin (Security): Make sure no examples encourage putting API keys in the compose file. Also, please ensure .env is ignored and that any mounted config is read-only.
Bruno Silva (author): Removed any inline env values; added .env.compose.example with placeholders only, confirmed .env is ignored, set config mounts to :ro where applicable.
Wei Chen (Docs): Can we add a single command path for new users (make compose-up) and a troubleshooting section for ‘unhealthy’ containers?
Bruno Silva (author): Added Make targets and a short troubleshooting section (common causes: Docker memory too low, ports in use, qdrant volume corruption; includes compose-reset).
Sahana Iyer (CI): Smoke job looks good, but please pin docker compose action versions and keep runtime <5 min. Also, avoid pulling large base images twice.
Bruno Silva (author): Pinned action versions and enabled buildx cache; smoke job now ~3m20s on CI.
